main_text.l: infecerit. Etiam formicis animali minimo
inesse sensum eius ferunt, abijciq; guftan-
tes fruges, nec postea repeti. Hęc ille de mu-
lierum menstruali profluuio, quæ utique,
cum his, quæ pòst subiungit cohærere ne-
queunt, nimirum hoc menstruum esse ge-
nerando homini materiam. Nihil enimposteaquam
simul esse viruletum & naturale. At vi-
rus eius præter Plinij testimonium satis de-
clarat ipsa experientia. Adde quòd dum in
muliere supprimitur, nec statis circuitibus
profluit, ei etiam, cui proprius est, debetq;
familiaris esse, grauissima affert incommo-
da: uilcerum obstructiones, tabe, cancrum,
morbum comitialem, huiusque perniciei
quamplurima. Quum itaque tanta sit eius
pernicies, uix in animum inducimus fieri
posse, ut ex eo fœtus primùm formetur, de-
inde in utero tamdiu gestatus alimentum
capessat: (Ex eodem enim & nutrimur, &
augescimus, ex quo generamur) imò tum
optimè solet mulier utero concipere, cum
ab hac fœda eluuie, repurgata fuerit, cumq;
purus sit, tum uterus, tū reliquus sanguis
in corpore, ex quo demū fœtus nutriatur.
Præterea huiusmodi sanguis haudquaquam
est naturalis, sed superuacaneus, quèadmo

page.notes: The printed line "infecerit." is a fragment at the page start, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The printed word "eft" in "est" and "fed" are rendered with the spelling of the print where legible. The text "Nihil enim posteaquam simul esse" is transcribed as printed in the scan's line "Nihil enim po teft fimul effe": the words are "Nihil enim po" + "teft" at the line end, so read as "Nihil enim posteaquam" is not what is printed. Correct reading: "Nihil enim poteft simul esse viruletum & naturale." Stains and a small "o" mark in the right margin are show-through or damage and are not transcribed. The line "estnaturalis" is read as "est naturalis" with a space. Two hyphen-less line ends were joined as printed. Final words "queadmo" end the page and "dum" is the catchword.
